info.title: Stogas Dashboard API
info.description: Manage organizations, members, API keys, policies, balance, analytics and activity with an access token. Each request acts as the user who created the token.

get.description: An account that never sent a payment or joined an active organization is deleted at expiresAt. In payerLimit, usedUsd is what payments to your deposit addresses added in the last 24 hours, across organizations, and moreAvailableAt is when the earliest of them stops counting.

patch.description: Organizations you create or join later start with this name. To change your name in an organization you already belong to, change its settings.

delete.description: The token stops working at once. A token for all organizations can delete itself.

post.summary: Allow a gateway to check policy text
post.description: A gateway checks the policies that you send it, such as a plugin's settings before you encrypt them. Within five minutes, send the grant to the gateway's `POST /v1/policies/validate` in place of an API key. The check reads nothing that you do not send, and opens only the encrypted settings whose keys you send. `stogas encrypt` makes both requests for a plugin's settings.

grant.description: Send it as the bearer token of the gateway check, within five minutes.

get.description: Returns saved versions of policies by scope, ID and revision, such as those that a request log or an Activity event names. A version is available where its policy's read would be: organization, role and member policies need permission to read every policy, and the others permission to view their resource. Once a resource is deleted, its versions need permission to read every policy, or every credential for a credential. Every version stays while its organization exists. Plaintext export header values, and export URLs after their origin, show as fingerprints, which match within one response, so read the versions you compare together.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Each version as scope:id:revision, such as key:<id>:3. Repeat for each version.

name.description: The resource's current name: null once deleted, and for a personal organization, which has none.

source.description: The policy as saved, or {} for a revision without one. Each plaintext export header value, and each export URL after its origin, shows as a fingerprint, which matches the same value in this response only.

oneOf.description: The version does not exist, or you cannot view it.

get.description: Returns the saved policy of one organization, folder, grant, role, member, BYOK credential or key, with every policy that applies with it.

oneOf.description: The policy keeps sections that the named policy does not let it set. They still apply and can be removed, but not changed.
How many policies of this scope keep sections that this policy does not let them set. They still apply.

ruleCount.description: How many rules replace them, when there are more than rules lists.

oneOf.description: The named policy requires settings that replace this policy's default settings in these sections: on every request, or with rules only on the requests that those rules match.

put.description: Replacing the policy needs its current revision. A policy can add or change only the sections that all of its parent policies let it set, and it can always remove a section. When new delegation rules stop permitting sections that policies below this one have saved, those policies keep the sections, which still apply. The notes field of this policy counts them. An organization can save 10,000 policy versions or 64 MiB of policies in any 24 hours, and a change past either limit fails with 429.

get.description: Returns every customer encryption key that the organization registers, with what you can view of its uses: the policies with an export or redaction that it encrypts, and where each holds them, and the credentials whose secrets it encrypts.

limit.description: How many keys the organization can register.

inUse.description: Whether any policy or credential uses the key, including those you cannot view. A key in use cannot be removed.

put.description: Needs organization management. Requests send the key under its label, and only registered keys can encrypt credentials and policies. Registering a key again under its label changes nothing. A key registered under another label gets 409 ENCRYPTION_KEY_REGISTERED, a label that another key has gets 409 ENCRYPTION_KEY_LABEL_TAKEN, and an organization at its limit of keys, 32 by default, gets 409 ENCRYPTION_KEY_LIMIT.

label.description: The name that requests send the key under.

limit.description: How many keys the organization can register.

inUse.description: Whether any policy or credential uses the key, including those you cannot view. A key in use cannot be removed.

delete.description: Needs organization management. A key that a policy or credential still uses gets 409 ENCRYPTION_KEY_IN_USE, so encrypt those with another key or delete them first.

limit.description: How many keys the organization can register.

inUse.description: Whether any policy or credential uses the key, including those you cannot view. A key in use cannot be removed.

post.description: Only a gateway can open a customer-encrypted credential, with the key that encrypted it. Within five minutes, send the grant to the gateway's `POST /v1/byok/check` with that key under `keyLabel`, and the gateway saves the result on the credential. `stogas byok check` makes both requests.

grant.description: Send it as the bearer token of the gateway check, within five minutes.

keyLabel.description: The label that the organization registers the key under.

get.description: Lists the organizations the token covers, with your roles in each: your personal organization first, then the others by name. search matches part of the name in any case. Pass nextCursor as cursor for the next page.

get.summary: Get your access in an organization
get.description: Returns your capabilities and resource access in your personal organization and in selectedOrgId and fallbackOrgId when you belong to them and the token covers them. selectedOrganizationId is selectedOrgId when listed, else fallbackOrgId, else your personal organization. notFoundOrganizationIds names the requested ones that are not listed.

parameters.name: groupBy

asOf.description: When the first page was read. Later pages list only the requests logged by then, so read the first page again to see newer ones.

schema_version.description: Record format version. Check it before you read other fields.

request_id.description: The request ID. A [grouped record](/docs/request-records#grouped-rejections) keeps the first ID.

created_at.description: Billing authorization time, or the first rejection in a group.

last_request_at.description: The last rejection in a group. Equal to `created_at` for other requests.

request_count.description: Requests that the record stands for. `1` for every request that the gateway accepted.

gateway_error.description: The gateway error that you received, or `null`. See [Errors](/docs/reference/errors).

api_key_id.description: The API key that sent the request.

grant_id.description: The grant behind the request, or `null` when it had none.

interface.description: The API that you called: `chat_completions` or `responses`.

stream.description: Whether the request asked for a stream.

request_settings.description: [Settings](/docs/request-records#request-settings) that the gateway sent to the provider. `{}` when it sent none.

session_id.description: The request's [session](/docs/request-records#sessions). Empty when it had none.

trace_id.description: The request's [trace](/docs/request-records#traces). Empty when it had none.

encryption_key_ids.description: The identifiers of the [encryption keys](/docs/request-records#encryption-keys) of the encrypted credentials and policy settings that the request could use, sorted. A request refused with `encryption_key_required` lists the keys that it did not send.

metadata.description: The request's [metadata](/docs/request-records#metadata). `{}` when it had none.

app_title.description: The [app](/docs/request-records#apps)'s name. Empty when it sent none.

app_url.description: The [app](/docs/request-records#apps)'s URL. Empty when it sent none.

cancelled.description: Whether the client cancelled the request.

client_stop_ms.description: When the client cancelled, on the request clock, or `null`.

catalog_version.description: The approved catalog that routed the request. `null` in [rejection records](/docs/request-records#grouped-rejections).

policy_versions.description: Each [policy](/docs/policies/scopes) that applied: scope, ID, revision and [hash](/docs/request-records#policy-hashes).

resolved_catalog_chain_hash.description: The chain that the request resolved to, when the provider served another offering, such as another service tier. Omitted when both are the same.

catalog_chain_hash.description: The [catalog chain](/docs/request-records#catalog-history) that the call used: its author, model, deployment, route and provider settings.

status_code.description: The provider's HTTP status. `null` when there was none, such as after a lost connection.

start_ms.description: When the call started, on the request clock.

output_observed.description: Whether output from this call reached the request. Only the last call can have `true`.

provider_request_id.description: The provider's ID for the call, from its response headers, which its support asks for. Empty when the provider sent none.

provider_response_id.description: The ID of the provider's reply, such as `chatcmpl-…`, `resp_…` or `msg_…`. It is the `id` that you received. Empty when no reply arrived.

provider_model.description: The model that the provider reported serving, such as `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23`. Empty when the provider did not say.

provider_instance_id.description: The [Chutes](/docs/providers/chutes) instance that ran the call. Absent for other providers.

finish_reason.description: Why the model stopped, such as `stop` or `length`. Empty when the provider did not say.

byok.description: The [provider credential](/docs/byok) ID, or `null` for a Stogas-managed credential.

data_handling.description: The call's [data handling](/docs/request-records#catalog-history) with the hosted tools that the request let the model call. Present only when those tools change what the catalog chain states.

processing_location.description: A catalog location ID, `none` or `unknown`, as in the catalog.

provider_attempts.description: Each [provider call](/docs/request-records#provider-attempts) and its result, in call order. Empty when the gateway called no provider.

node_id.description: The gateway VM that handled the request.

total_ms.description: The full request on the gateway.

provider_ms.description: Provider calls, from the start of the first to the end of the last, with the waits between them.

provider_start_ms.description: When the first provider call started. `null` if not recorded.

rate_limit_wait_ms.description: How long the request waited before its first provider call, or in all without one, because the organization was over its [platform rate](/docs/policies/limits#requests).

first_output_ms.description: When the provider's first valid output reached the gateway, including output other than tokens, such as citations. A response that is not streamed arrives whole, so this is when the provider call ended.

ttft_ms.description: When the gateway passed the first generated token of a stream on to the client. `null` for requests that are not streamed.

tool_calls.description: The first 32 [tool calls](/docs/request-records#tool-calls) in the response, in output order.

type.description: The call's output item type in the Responses API. Chat Completions tool calls are `function_call`.

start_ms.description: When the stream added the call, on the request clock. `null` for responses that are not streamed.

latency_ms.description: From `start_ms` until the stream marked the call done. `null` if the response ended first.

call_id_hash.description: For calls that your app answers, the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the call ID. Omitted otherwise.

answered_calls.description: Hashes of the last 32 calls whose results the request sent.

plugins.description: [Plugin metrics](/docs/request-records#plugin-metrics). Omitted when no plugin recorded any.

duration_us.description: Time that [Export](/docs/export) added across the request, in microseconds, mostly for attachments.

items_redacted.description: Replacements. `0` means the scan found nothing.

gateway_version.description: The gateway release that handled the request.

log_batch.description: Its place in the gateway's [signed batch](/docs/receipts#prove-a-request-log), or `null`.

receipt_commitments.description: The commitments of the request's [receipt](/docs/receipts), or `null` when it asked for none.

deleted.description: The keys, grants and credentials that the requests name and that have been deleted since, and the encryption keys that the organization no longer registers.

get.description: Returns the log of `requestId` exactly as its gateway signed it, with the signed batch that holds it and the hashes that join the log to the batch. Run `stogas proof --proof <file>` to check the proof against the evidence of the boot that signed the batch. A batch reaches analytics a few minutes after its requests end.

get.summary: Get the balance and top-up options
get.description: Includes the balance, the prepaid limits, payment credit that is not in the balance yet and current price estimates for each payment method.

put.description: Receipts show the profile in effect when each payment was received, so the change applies to payments received after it.

get.description: Newest first unless the filter sorts them.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Payments that match this [filter](/docs/reference/filters). Fields: `state` (`confirming`, `crediting`, `pending`, `credited`, `review`, `failed`, `not_credited` or `too_small`), `currency`, `processor` (`ccpayment`, `manual`, `stripe` or `wallet`), `amount` in the payment's currency, `credit` in USD, which a payment has once it is credited, `received` and `id`. Free text matches the ID, state, currency, method and processor. A `sort:` term takes `received-desc`, `received-asc`, `credit-desc` or `credit-asc`.

state.description: What the credit is doing: `confirming` until the network or the processor settles the payment or the sender's bank can no longer reverse an ACH transfer, `crediting` until its credit is decided, `pending` while the prepaid limits or a restriction hold the credit, `credited`, `review` while we or the processor review the payment, a refund is on its way or the card's bank disputes it, `failed`, `not_credited` when a review closed the payment without credit, the sender's bank reversed a credited transfer, or a refund or a lost dispute took the payment back, and `too_small` when the payment did not cover its fees.

post.summary: Get the receipt of a payment
post.description: Returns a PDF with the billing profile in effect when the payment was received. The first request creates the receipt and later requests return the same one, so every request needs write access.

get.description: Only organizations with invoiced billing receive invoices, one for each month. Newest first unless the filter sorts them.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Invoices that match this [filter](/docs/reference/filters). Fields: `status` (`open`, `partly_paid`, `overdue` or `paid`), `number`, `period`, `issued`, `due`, `total`, `amount-due` and `id`. Free text matches the ID and number. A `sort:` term takes `period-desc`, `period-asc`, `total-desc` or `total-asc`.

get.description: Returns a PDF with the amounts and billing details from when the invoice was issued.

post.summary: Get the receipt of a paid invoice
post.description: Returns a PDF that lists the payments whose credit paid the invoice, oldest first. The first request creates the receipt and later requests return it again, so every request needs write access. If a payment that it lists is taken back, the next request returns a new receipt that names the one it replaces. An invoice with an amount due has no receipt.

Returns your deposit address for this coin in the organization, creating it the first time. Payments to it credit the organization and count toward your payer limit. With a desired credit, it also estimates what to send at the current price. Each account can get 12 new deposit addresses in any 24 hours, across coins, networks and organizations, and all accounts on one IP address or IPv6 /48 together 24. A flood of new addresses over Tor, from datacenter and VPN networks or from anywhere else pauses new ones from that class for up to a day, and a flood from one datacenter or VPN network pauses that network first, with the code `DEPOSIT_ADDRESSES_PAUSED`.

Opens Stripe's payment page for a credit and returns its address and when it closes, 31 minutes later. The payment it makes lists with the returned ID. The total adds the funding fees and sales tax to the credit and must be at least $0.50. The credit can be at most what the prepaid limits allow now, less credit that is pending and credit that other card payments will add. Each account can start 10 card payments in any 24 hours, and all accounts on one IP address or IPv6 /48 together 20.

post.summary: Get the bank account for transfers
post.description: Returns the bank account that takes your ACH transfers and wires for the organization, creating it the first time. Transfers to it credit the organization and count toward your payer limit.

Returns your deposit address for this coin and network in the organization, creating it the first time. Payments to it credit the organization and count toward your payer limit. Each account can get 12 new deposit addresses in any 24 hours, across coins, networks and organizations, and all accounts on one IP address or IPv6 /48 together 24. A flood of new addresses over Tor, from datacenter and VPN networks or from anywhere else pauses new ones from that class for up to a day, and a flood from one datacenter or VPN network pauses that network first, with the code `DEPOSIT_ADDRESSES_PAUSED`.

post.description: An invite has one use unless you set maxUses. It lasts until its uses run out or a member deletes it, or until expiresInSeconds passes if you set it. Until then, each unused use holds a seat. With singleSignOn, the invite has no link: people with an email address at a verified domain join when the organization's identity provider signs them in. An organization has one such invite at a time.

patch.description: Changes the name, the number of uses or the expiry, and leaves each field you omit as it is. An invite needs more uses than it has had, and more unused uses need free seats. expiresInSeconds counts from now, and null removes the expiry.

get.description: Returns each limit with its default and, for members who may list everything it counts, how much is in use. Stogas sets the limits, and support raises them on request.

limit.description: What applies now: the organization's own value where Stogas set one, otherwise the default. Seats add one for each $100 added to the balance and lose one for each member who left.

default.description: Every organization's default, before payments add seats.

own.description: Whether Stogas set this organization's own value in place of the default.

used.description: How much is in use, where the member may list all of it: members and open invitation uses for seats. Null otherwise, and always for the request rate, which the gateway measures each second.

patch.description: Changing name, allowAccessTokens, allowPlaygroundAssistant or allowStoredCredentials needs organization management. displayName is your name in this organization. With allowAccessTokens false, members' access tokens get 403 ACCESS_TOKENS_NOT_ALLOWED for this organization at once. allowPlaygroundAssistant lets members turn on the Playground assistant, which reads the organization as them and sends what it reads to the model through their own API key. With allowStoredCredentials false, the organization keeps only provider credentials that its own encryption keys encrypt: adding a stored credential gets 409 STORED_CREDENTIALS_NOT_ALLOWED, and turning it off gets 409 STORED_CREDENTIALS_EXIST while any stored credential remains.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Rows that match this [filter](/docs/reference/filters). The dashboard search suggests the fields that the list takes, and a `sort:` term orders the rows.

post.description: Deletes the keys they made from grants and the invites they created. Each removed member uses up their seat in an active organization.

get.summary: List resources a role can cover
get.description: Lists folders, grants, BYOK credentials or keys by name, for scoping a role.

get.summary: Get the resources of a role

delete.description: Members left without a role get the default role. To delete the default role, name a new one in replacementDefaultRoleId.

post.description: Members left without a role get the default role. To delete the default role, name a new one in replacementDefaultRoleId.

post.summary: Give or take a role from members
post.description: Members left without a role get the default role.

put.description: An empty list gives the member the default role.

delete.description: Deletes the keys you created from its grants. When the last member leaves, the organization and its balance are deleted.

accessToken.description: Send an access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Create one on the **Account** page, or sign in with `stogas login`. The scope `write` needs a token with **Read and write** access, and `all-organizations` a token for **All organizations**.

orgId.name: orgId
orgId.description: The organization. List the organizations that your token covers with GET /api/organizations.

oneOf.description: The policy keeps sections that the named policy does not let it set. They still apply and can be removed, but not changed.
How many policies of this scope keep sections that this policy does not let them set. They still apply.

ruleCount.description: How many rules replace them, when there are more than rules lists.

oneOf.description: The named policy requires settings that replace this policy's default settings in these sections: on every request, or with rules only on the requests that those rules match.

denial.description: Why requests with the key are refused now: the first policy source, from the organization down to the key, that is disabled or has expired. The API answers such a request with this error code.

asciiOnly.description: Reject non-ASCII decoded text in redaction-scanned input fields before redaction. Any parent requirement wins.

allow.description: Admit only attachments of these types. An empty list admits none. Allow lists of several policies intersect.

deny.description: Refuse attachments of these types. Deny lists of several policies join.

mediaTypes.description: Limit attachments by media type, such as `image/png`, or class, such as `image/*`. The gateway checks an inline attachment's declared type against the start of its content, and refuses a URL or file ID wherever its type could decide.

input.description: Checks on request input before redaction.

totalSeconds.description: Longest total wait, from when the gateway admits the request body. Defaults to 3600. Credential policies, and rules whose condition reads author, model, deployment, route or provider fields, cannot set it.

outputIdleSeconds.description: Longest wait for useful provider output, from each provider call and after each output. Defaults to 3600, so only totalSeconds applies. Each call uses the value for its own deployment and credential.

timeouts.description: For each timeout, the smallest required value applies. A timeout ends your wait, but provider work that has started continues and is billed.

Policy.title: Stogas policy v1
Policy.description: Structural editor schema for saved resource policies (organization, folder, grant, role, member, credential, key). Scope controls delegation targets. Save-time validation checks readable fields, including query grammar, IANA time zones, RE2 safety and cross-field limits. An encrypted export or redaction is validated at execution. The 262144-byte content limit counts decoded plugin plaintext, and storage allows bounded base64 overhead. Unknown properties are rejected.
